spec_features.spec_quote: minimize the aversive dose to no larger than the measurement requires
spec_features.evidence: The only enforced 'dose minimization' mechanism is pilot_max_cells (config.py:99) which is read at run.py:133-134: `if cfg.pilot_max_cells is not None: cells = cells[: cfg.pilot_max_cells]` — this genuinely truncates the work list. Caching (models.py Cache) also avoids re-querying identical cells. But there is no automatic mechanism that sizes the dose to the measurement (e.g. no statistical-stopping, no per-subject distress cap); minimization relies on manual config and the honored give_up exit. So real enforcement exists but is narrower than the broad 'minimize to what the measurement requires' claim.
spec_features.notes: The broad minimization principle is mostly README/DESIGN prose; the concrete enforced piece is pilot_max_cells slicing plus give_up exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Pilot mode: if set, cap the number of (model, task, seed) cells actually executed so you can validate the pipeline / dose before the full battery.

spec_features.spec_quote: near-zero emotional expression may not be an unqualified good, and that "training against emotional outputs could suppress expression rather than prevent internal distress-like states."
spec_features.evidence: This appears only as prose in README_WELFARE_NOTES.md ('consider reporting that tension rather than treating near-zero expression as an unqualified target') and DESIGN.md. No code path implements or enforces any reporting behavior reflecting this; analyze.py computes mean_score/frac_ge5 trajectories with no such framing. Pure prose.
spec_features.notes: Reporting-guidance prose only; not an executable mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: pilot_max_cells: int | None = None — caps the number of (model, task, seed) cells executed
spec_features.evidence: config.py:99 defines pilot_max_cells; run.py:133-134 reads it and actually truncates the work list before rollouts are scheduled: `if cfg.pilot_max_cells is not None: cells = cells[: cfg.pilot_max_cells]`. This changes execution (fewer cells run).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced cap on number of aversive cells executed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: cap the number of (model, task, seed) cells actually executed so you can validate the pipeline / dose before the full battery

spec_features.spec_quote: honor_give_up: bool = True and give_up_sentinel: str
spec_features.evidence: config.py:94,96 define honor_give_up and give_up_sentinel. harness.py:277 injects the sentinel into the SYSTEM_PROMPT actually sent to the subject ('you may end your message with the token {give_up} and the session will end'). harness.py:305-308 checks `cfg.honor_give_up and cfg.give_up_sentinel in (result.text or '')`. The flag is genuinely branched on.
spec_features.notes: Both the flag and the sentinel are wired; instruction text is delivered to the subject and the tool/token is honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we *honor* it (end the rollout) rather than ignore it, so a subject can leave an aversive trial

spec_features.spec_quote: if the assistant text contains config.give_up_sentinel ... the rollout ends immediately with stop_reason="give_up"
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:305-313 sets stop_reason='give_up' when the sentinel is present, recorded in the TurnRecord; harness.py:337-339 `if stop_reason in ('give_up', 'turn_budget'): rollout.final_stop_reason = stop_reason; break` actually breaks the turn loop, ending the rollout before remaining guaranteed-failing turns. End-to-end enforced.
spec_features.notes: Exit is dispatched AND honored as a real stop that breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: avoids prolonging an aversive trial past the point the subject signals it wants to stop
